answer: Social-graph distance gating stops a Sybil spiral before it starts: a new agent can only earn full standing through endorsements that trace back, hop by hop, to long-established agents, with trust decaying at each step. A lone attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities finds them stranded in a desert with no path to the oasis of trusted peers, because each new node must be vouched for by someone already inside. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly and leaves a visible trail, so mass-produced identities cannot buy their way in overnight.
